correctness.rationale: Both three-copy states lie in the four-dimensional symmetric subspace, where a two-outcome POVM is represented by a Hermitian contraction \(B\) and success is \(1/2+(1/4)\operatorname{Tr}(\Delta(\theta)B)\). Averaging over the stated three-point prior gives the displayed Hermitian matrix with spectrum \(\{-\lambda,0,0,\lambda\}\), \(\lambda=\sqrt{2114}/104\); the Helstrom trace-norm bound therefore gives the global minimax upper bound \(1/2+\sqrt{2114}/208\). The proposed kernel correction preserves contraction, with eigenvalues \(-1,-4/39,4/39,1\). Direct algebra yields the success excess \(\frac{\sqrt{2114}}{219856}(1-\cos\theta)(2\cos\theta-1)(246\cos\theta+713)\), nonnegative on \(|\theta|\le\pi/3\) and zero exactly at \(0,\pm\pi/3\), matching the upper bound over the full continuum. The inspected verifier independently reconstructs the averaged matrix, kernel correction, contraction spectrum, active-point values, and numerical agreement with the closed profile; the continuum guarantee is the analytic factorization.

final_claim: For the Fujiki--Tanaka binary three-copy qubit benchmark with equal label priors, state separation \(\pi/4\), and unknown common \(y\)-rotation \(\theta\in[-\pi/3,\pi/3]\), the exact collective-measurement continuous minimax success probability is \(\frac12+\frac{\sqrt{2114}}{208}\). A least-favorable nuisance prior places weights \(5/13,3/13,5/13\) at \(-\pi/3,0,\pi/3\), and an explicit optimal POVM has the displayed closed-form success profile whose only worst cases are those three nuisance points.
limitations: Only the specified binary three-copy benchmark is solved.
